experiments.name: Cryogenic dark/pinhole characterization of a Teledyne HAWAII-2RG (2048x2048 HgCdTe) infrared array held at 35 K in a closed-cycle test cryostat at ~10 microTorr

experiments.description: QUBIC TES focal-plane tests: 256 NbSi transition-edge sensors (Tc ~410 mK) cooled to ~320 mK by a He-3 fridge in a pulse-tube cryostat, read out by 128 SQUIDs at 1 K inside a magnetic shield and a cryogenic SiGe ASIC at ~40 K; Tc, I-V, P-T and NEP are measured, with dark-pixel Tc first measured in an Oxford Instruments dilution fridge. The focal plane is 110 mm in diameter.

experiments.description: Transition-edge-sensor x-ray microcalorimeter arrays for the Lynx X-ray Microcalorimeter are characterized (R-T, pulses, energy resolution with Al/Mn K-alpha) on a sub-100 mK bath: a 4.5 K cryocooler stage plus a multistage ADR to ~50 mK; the first UHR array, with Tc ~10 mK below the 65 mK target, had to be run at a 42 mK bath. TESs require careful magnetic shielding, and multiplexed readout uses microwave SQUID resonators with a 4-8 GHz HEMT at ~4 K.

requirements.rationale: The UHR array had to be characterized at a 42 mK bath temperature (nominal 50 mK).

experiments.name: Cryogenic L-band (1.2-1.8 GHz) receiver front end for FAST: OMT at 55 K and Coupling-LNAs at 15 K in a GM-cooled rectangular dewar at 1e-5 Pa behind a film vacuum window
experiments.plain_name: Cool a giant radio telescope's 1.2-1.8 GHz receiver electronics to 15 K to cut its noise
experiments.description: The FAST single-beam L-band receiver: a 728.3 mm long conical quad-ridge OMT (189 mm internal aperture) is cooled by the first GM stage to ~55 K and two Coupling-LNAs (noise ~4 K) by the second stage to 15 K inside a rectangular vacuum dewar reaching 1e-5 Pa; the RF enters through a polyimide/Teflon film window. LNA noise at 15 K is measured with the Variable Load Temperature method and the receiver noise (<9 K) with hot/cold loads.

requirements.rationale: The Coupling-LNAs must operate at a physical temperature of 15 K.
requirements.document_title: Ultra-Low Noise L-Band Cryogenic Astronomical Receiver for FAST Telescope (Liu et al., Res. Astron. Astrophys., arXiv:2103.10677)
requirements.quote: Amplification and coupling function circuits are integrated as a single Coupling-LNA with full noise temperature of 4 K at the physical temperature of 15 K.

requirements.rationale: The dewar reaches a vacuum of 1e-5 Pa to suppress gas conduction and convection to the cold parts.
requirements.document_title: Ultra-Low Noise L-Band Cryogenic Astronomical Receiver for FAST Telescope (Liu et al., Res. Astron. Astrophys., arXiv:2103.10677)
requirements.quote: The heat insulation gap, vacuum degree of 10-5 Pa and thermal radiation shield will effectively eliminate the effects of conduction, convection and radiation of heats from dewar walls to cryogenic parts.

requirements.rationale: The OMT and LNAs sit inside a vacuum dewar.
requirements.document_title: Ultra-Low Noise L-Band Cryogenic Astronomical Receiver for FAST Telescope (Liu et al., Res. Astron. Astrophys., arXiv:2103.10677)
requirements.quote: The cryogenic cooling unit basing on GM cycle (Thirumaleshwar & Subramanyam 1986) is built to provide vacuum and cryogenic environment for low noise microwave parts in the frontend of receiver.

requirements.rationale: The sky signal enters the dewar through a large film vacuum window in front of the OMT.

requirements.quote: Polyimide and Teflon bilayers films with Fluorine rubber sealing rings are used to seal vacuum window in view of rather large window diameter corresponding to OMT in L-band

experiments.name: Wideband (2.5-14 GHz) cryogenic feed receiver: quad-ridged flared horn, high-pass filter, noise coupler and LNAs cooled to 15 K in a GM cryostat with Mylar RF window; Y-factor receiver temperature with 295 K absorber
experiments.plain_name: Cool an entire radio antenna feed horn to 15 K and measure how much noise it adds
experiments.description: Arecibo 12 m telescope receiver: the QRFH, 2.5 GHz high-pass filters, noise couplers and Citcryo1-12D LNAs are enclosed in a cryostat built around a two-stage GM cryocooler (Trillium 350CS cold head, M600 compressor) and cooled to 15 K; signals enter through a Mylar window under a dry-air radome; receiver temperature (median 25 K over 2.5-14 GHz) is measured by the Y-factor method with a 295 K absorber as hot load and the sky as cold load.

requirements.rationale: The horn, filter, coupler and LNA are cooled to 15 K.
requirements.document_title: A Cryogenic Wideband (2.5 - 14 GHz) Receiver system for the Arecibo 12m Telescope (Roshi et al., Radio Science, arXiv:2308.05826)
requirements.quote: The QRHF, highpass filter, noise coupler and LNA are located inside a cryostat and are cooled to 15 K.

requirements.rationale: Sky and hot-load radiation reach the cold horn through the cryostat RF window (Mylar).
requirements.document_title: A Cryogenic Wideband (2.5 - 14 GHz) Receiver system for the Arecibo 12m Telescope (Roshi et al., Radio Science, arXiv:2308.05826)
requirements.quote: Due to the relatively high humidity at Arecibo, we built a radome with Mylar material in front of the cryostat radio frequency window.

requirements.rationale: The cold RF chain must carry 2.5-14 GHz.
